html:
Norway is a kingdom along the western and northern coast of Scandinavia. The map shows it as an independent medieval kingdom from 1100 to 1300, and as a modern state from 1914 to 2010. In between it was joined to Denmark and then to Sweden.

According to the sagas Harald Fairhair first united the coast around 872, building on the Viking-age kingdom. Olaf II pushed Christianity and was killed at the Battle of Stiklestad in 1030; he became Norway's patron saint. A long civil war in the 1100s ended under Haakon IV, whose reign was a high point. In 1262 to 1264 the Icelandic Commonwealth and Greenland accepted the Norwegian king.

The Black Death of 1349 killed perhaps half the people and weakened the old nobility. By marriage Norway came under the Danish king in 1380 and then into the Kalmar Union. For four centuries it was the junior partner in Denmark-Norway, ruled from Copenhagen.

In 1814 Denmark had to give Norway to Sweden. The Norwegians wrote the Constitution of 1814, still in force, and kept their own parliament inside the union of Sweden-Norway. They left peacefully in 1905. Germany occupied Norway from 1940 to 1945. Oil found in the North Sea in 1969 made it one of the richest countries in the world; it saves the profits in a state fund. Its voters twice rejected joining the European Union, in 1972 and 1994.
sum: Norway is a kingdom along the western and northern coast of Scandinavia. The map shows it as an independent medieval kingdom from 1100 to 1300, and as a modern state from 1914 to 2010. In between it was joined to Denmark and then to Sweden.
